summary: Google supports OAuth 2.0 for sign-in and API access, and the basics are quick. The hard part is verification: the moment you ask for sensitive scopes (Gmail, Drive, Calendar), Google wants to review your app before strangers can use it without a scary warning screen.

rationale: Creating the OAuth client itself is easy - the weight comes from Google's verification program.
Sensitive scopes trigger mandatory verification with a written justification per scope, a demo video, and a verified domain.
Restricted scopes (reading Gmail, for example) add a third-party security assessment on top.

timeEstimate.setup: About an hour to create the project, configure the consent screen and get a working client ID.
timeEstimate.approval: A few days to several weeks for verification, depending on scopes; restricted-scope security assessments can run longer.

basis.text: Verification steps and the unverified-app warning are described in Google's OAuth verification help.
No fixed SLA is published for verification, so treat any timeline as an estimate.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project
steps.detail: In Google Cloud Console, create a project, then open APIs & Services > OAuth consent screen. Fill in the app name, support email, homepage and privacy policy links.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client
steps.detail: Under APIs & Services > Credentials, create an OAuth 2.0 Client ID (Web application) and register your redirect URIs. Keep the client secret server-side.

steps.title: Stay in Testing while you build
steps.detail: While the consent screen is in Testing, only test users you list can sign in, and their refresh tokens expire after 7 days. Fine for development; not for real users.

steps.title: Submit for verification before launch
steps.detail: Switch publishing status to In production and submit. For sensitive scopes, write a plain-English justification for each scope and record a short video showing exactly how the app uses them. Verify ownership of your domain in Search Console.

steps.title: Answer the reviewer's questions
steps.detail: Google's review team replies by email and often asks for changes. Each round adds days, so the first submission should be complete.

requirements.item: A Google account and a Google Cloud project
A public homepage and privacy policy on a domain you own (verified in Search Console)
A demo video and per-scope justifications if you use sensitive scopes

gotchas.text: Unverified apps show a warning screen and are capped at 100 test users - new users simply can't get through.
Adding a sensitive scope later means re-verification.
Refresh tokens for test users expire after 7 days in Testing mode, which looks like a bug if you don't know it's coming.

agentCanDo: Read Google's current OAuth and verification docs and keep this guide fresh
Map the scopes you need to Google's sensitive/restricted categories
Draft the per-scope justifications and the verification checklist
developerMustDo: Own the Google account, the Cloud project and the domain
Record the demo video and submit the verification form
Reply to Google's review team and make requested changes
